results.title: Stable atoms are exactly what diagonal separation requires
results.statement: Separation of propositions by diagonal characters is equivalent over C to ND (type t) together with Atomicity (type t).

results.title: Endpoint separation and boxed Infinitary Comprehension reconstruct full standard models over λ-free H
results.statement: Over the specified λ-free classical typed applicative base, full typed endpoint separation and boxed Infinitary Comprehension characterize the full standard relational hierarchies among set-sized models, up to canonical typed representation, in ZF. Finite comprehension instances reconstruct abstraction and C; separation supplies Intensionality, Functionality and C5, after which Atomicity and the full representation follow. The initial observer qualification can omit translated equality clauses. Whole-operation preservation has an equivalent λ-free formulation using composite representatives.

The selected axioms are closed under theorem necessitation. Abstraction, Intensionality and independently represented logical objects are not premises. Endpoint separation ranges over every relational type and finite tested-type list, with endpoint range, explicit Top-fixing and strict Boolean/quantifier identities. Infinitary comprehension allows arbitrary set-indexed simultaneous parameter families, including input type e, and finite bound argument tuples. Implication and biconditional are Boolean abbreviations.

results.title: Theoremhood and model construction have successive jump thresholds
results.statement:
The positive theories, Max and SP occupy three successive levels of computational strength.

| Pure theory | Theoremhood | Oracles computing some adequate countable model |
|---|---|---|
| C + ☐Plenitude + Axiom of Infinity (types e and t) | $\Sigma^0_1$-complete | PA degrees |
| C + ☐Functional Choice + Axiom of Infinity (types e and t) | $\Sigma^0_1$-complete | PA degrees |
| Max | $\Sigma^0_2$-complete | PA degrees over $0'$ |
| SP, **if consistent** | $\Sigma^0_3$-complete | PA degrees over $0''$ |

Adequate codes provide term interpretation and actual truth. PA degree over an oracle means the ability to compute a binary diagonally nonrecursive function relative to it; ordinary PA degrees use no oracle. The positive bounds already hold with the weaker Infinity schema at one admitted type. The theoremhood classifications persist under consistent extensions enumerable in the corresponding oracle.
results.scope: The original pure finitary relational language and fixed reference C are used throughout. Completeness is under ordinary computable many-one reductions. Model capacity means computing some countable BBK model with sorted domains, equality, uniform finite-term interpretation and actual truth. No bound for a bare action/category presentation is inferred. All SP existence and complexity conclusions require Con(SP).
results.significance: Arithmetic conservation does not erase the computational gaps between the positive packages, Max and SP. Theoremhood and selecting a complete model are different computational problems.

results.title: A complete theory has a model of exactly its computational degree
results.statement: From any supplied complete consistent pure theory Γ extending C, one can uniformly construct a countable BBK model whose complete pure theory is exactly Γ and whose adequate code has exactly Γ’s Turing degree. Consequently the positive and Max bounds above describe the exact degrees realized by models, not merely the oracles from which some model can be computed.
results.scope: The positive exact-degree theorem applies to any fixed consistent c.e. extension of C plus the Infinity schema at an admitted type; the Max theorem to any fixed consistent 0′-c.e. theory entailing pure Max. Degrees range across all models of the theory, not copies of one fixed structure. Codes contain canonical operational data and actual truth, without unrelated padding. No standardness or full-domain conclusion is asserted.
results.significance: The passage from a supplied complete theory to a model introduces no extra computational strength. The converse coding recovers information from original pure truth values.

results.title: Standard natural numbers impose a much stronger computational barrier
results.statement: Every adequate code of a C-model satisfying numerical noncollapse at σ and having externally standard Frege numbers at σ computes every hyperarithmetical real, and is itself nonhyperarithmetical. For any theory enumerable in a hyperarithmetical oracle with those arithmetic premises, if a standard model exists, some standard codes lie strictly below Kleene’s O; exactly the hyperarithmetical reals are computable from every standard code, and there is no least solution degree. For the specified positive and Max standard-number model classes, finite-condition satisfiability is Σ¹₁-complete and validity is Π¹₁-complete.
results.scope: Numerical noncollapse is Iσ = ◇I*σ in the cited notes. Standardness means that the actual number domain consists exactly of the distinct standard numeral denotations; it is a semantic restriction, not a finitary axiom. Standard models are supplied for the positive packages with the specified Infinity assumptions and for Max. An SP application requires existence of a standard SP model, not merely Con(SP). The analytic-completeness result uses the separate branch-graph constructions for the positive and Max classes; it is not asserted for every hyperarithmetically enumerable theory.
results.significance: Low unrestricted models and standard-number models have sharply different complexity. No fixed hyperarithmetical oracle can uniformly turn arbitrary adequate models into standard ones.

results.title: Finite descriptions distinguish the completion spaces
results.statement: In the space of complete consistent pure C-theories, Max forms a nonempty closed nowhere-dense set: every consistent finite description admits a refinement violating Max. C + ☐Plenitude forms a clopen set. For either C + ☐Plenitude or C + ☐Functional Choice, isolated completions are exactly the full Gallin theories with finite individual and world domains; removing those points leaves a perfect space with dense low completions. More generally, any consistent computably enumerable pure-complete extension of C fixes finite actual domains at every type, with recursively computable exact sizes and necessary finite bounds.
results.scope: Basic open sets specify finitely many pure sentences. The completion-space claims use general Henkin/BBK semantics, not full-semantics compactness. The positive isolated-point classification is stated without imposing Infinity; the positive infinite part and Max are each abstractly homeomorphic to Cantor space despite their different positions in the ambient space. Necessary finite bounds need not equal the exact actual sizes and do not by themselves yield C5.
results.significance: The comparison explains what finite descriptions can fix, and why the Max obstruction is stronger than the familiar failure of effective axiomatization.

Conjoining separately separating classes can be strictly weaker than requiring one class to satisfy both qualifications. The accompanying representation theorems characterize the connective, quantifier and equality branches with their explicit premises. Reversible accepting/rejecting meet separation plus one atom makes atoms separate order, represents every proposition as the join of its atoms, and gives a unique true atom. Under internal Frege finiteness of all propositions, material and pointwise meet separation are equivalent, and likewise for join separation, retaining each acceptance/rejection orientation. Full relational separation collapses all three tiers. A least true meet element or greatest false join element suffices for the corresponding normalization without finiteness. Reversible meet separation plus one atom is exactly bounded atomistic meet structure, a true atom and transitivity of admitted full-meet automorphisms on atoms; arbitrary extra restrictions use the exact MoveTrue condition without closure assumptions. A six-element model shows that atomisticity and a true atom alone do not suffice. For each finite preservation signature, pointwise separation is equivalent to the existence of an admitted composition-closed separating family of material observers, equivalently such a composition-closed family containing identity. Finite-image material meet separation is equivalent to at-most-two-output pointwise meet separation, and likewise for join, without finiteness of the proposition domain. Full typed OS need not imply ☐BF or ☐Functionality. Endpoint logical separation is equivalent to C5 + ☐OS + one atom, and already to C5 plus the boxed propositional Good_{ {t} } separation instance plus one atom. Reversible logical separation implies C5 + ☐OS + No Pure Contingency, with no atom or Actuality premise. The proof extends qualified involutions by typewise conjugation and applies separation to each closed pure sentence. Reversible logical separation is strictly stronger than C5 + ☐OS, even among atomless models: the even-block/power-of-two-block symmetry model has necessary OS but a contingent closed pure six-element selection sentence. Over H + ND (type t), material and pointwise meet/universal separation have the same exact meet/GLB representation, with a dual join/existential result. Finite-image normalization extends to matching quantifiers and joint M,V,Q,P packages. Over C, an admitted whole inverse is equivalent to necessary bijectivity; invertible Q_t observers are automatically Boolean. Local stabilizer conjugacy supplies reversible observers in the stated symmetry-model families. Internal Frege finiteness also gives exact affine representation by two-output pointwise homomorphisms, separately for XOR and biconditional. Plenitude at (t,t), stated explicitly over H, normalizes all seven nonempty primitive connective signatures, each affine operation, and the verified matching lattice/quantifier packages, including infinite-image observers. Full qualified right-inverse separation is exactly Rev. Qualified left-inverse separation is strictly weaker even with C5 and its own boxed schema; it implies OS, but not C5, ☐OS, its own boxed schema, ☐BF or ☐Functionality. The ternary Cantor model satisfies the separate endpoint-fixing M/Q/P, V/Q/P and N/Q/P separation schemas and their boxes, together with C and boxed BF and Functionality, while even propositional Boolean separation fails. Both arrows Rev ⇒ SplitMono ⇒ OS are strict. The full fork satisfies ☐OS and all boxed BF and Functionality but fails SplitMono, so SplitMono and ☐OS are incomparable. The full-H form is full OS plus the external schema RevSep(t,Δ) or KΔ. The condition D_t that every admitted injective E:tt is onto makes full SplitMono and Rev equivalent. It is strictly weaker than internal Frege finiteness: a two-colour finite-pinning model satisfies C5 + Rev + D_t with atomless propositions, while endpoint separation and internal Frege finiteness fail. results.notes: Only the finite independent primitive family is completely classified. Remaining comparisons concern infinite nonprincipal material-versus-pointwise M/V separation outside the proved sufficient hypotheses; bare-H infinite affine character existence without an admission premise; further partial-signature reversibility; further boxed inverse comparisons and intrinsic atomless-meet characterizations; and the narrower first-order endpoint-parameter noncontingency converse for Rev. Zorn supplies admitted characters; Plenitude supplies normalization and the specified involutive witnesses. Pointed and relative maximality characterize separation and partial-character extension respectively, without a converse to general Zorn. The parameter theorem covers finitely many individual and endpoint-valued first-order relation parameters, not arbitrary higher-type parameters. Internal finiteness, whole-operation identities and explicit H premises retain their stated scope. Zorn supplies both affine and lattice partial-character extension. D_t collapses the inverse comparison but not the endpoint comparison; the atomless two-colour model proves the latter failure. The atomless region includes exact gap, convex-block and finite-factor criteria under their stated structural hypotheses. SurjSep ⇒ ☐OS and SurjSep ⇒ ☐SurjSep are refuted; The root truth-profile countermodel retains ☐BF; the integer-shift predecessor separately refutes SurjSep ⇒ ☐BF at every admitted type.

groups.title: Quantified Infinity at all types reduces to two base types
groups.summary:
Over C, Axiom of Infinity (type t) is equivalent to Axiom of Infinity at every relational type. Adding Axiom of Infinity (type e) gives the schema at every admitted type. These are ordinary consequences of the certified downward finiteness theorem.

Under the relevant Functionality instances, finiteness at a relational type is equivalent to finiteness at t when the type contains no e, and to finiteness at both e and t otherwise. The countermodels explain why upward finiteness needs the extra assumption.

groups.title: Infinity schemata do not imply their quantified axioms, even with necessary Choice

sections.title: Continuum Hypothesis and forcing
sections.headline: CH variation, Maximalism, forcing transfer and Forcing Possibilism.

groups.title: CH can vary despite boxed structural principles
groups.summary: Assuming Con(ZFC), CH varies in a model satisfying ☐Atomicity, ☐BF, ☐Strong Leibniz, ☐Rigid Rigidity, ☐Weakly Rigid Weak Rigidity, ☐Tame Rigidity and Modal Well-Ordering together. All the relational schemata hold at every admitted relational type; BF and Well-Ordering include e. The two possible real structures disagree at the same type e. The component construction needs neither transitive set models nor standard natural numbers.

groups.title: Maximalism is incompatible with Non-contingency of CH
groups.summary:
Assuming Con(ZFC), the separate C-consistency of real structures satisfying CH and its negation gives

$$
\operatorname{Max}(C)+\text{Non-contingency of CH}\ \vdash\ \bot.
$$

Maximalism makes both real-structure assertions possible at the same type $e$.

groups.title: The full modalized cloud realizes both sides of CH
groups.summary: In the specified full modalized-domain construction, finite relational types correspond to their Boolean-valued counterparts. The resulting lottery cloud makes both CH and its negation possible for real structures at the same type et. This is a theorem about that full construction, not a consequence established for the proposed abstract modal axioms alone.

groups.title: Strict-smallness Forcing Possibilism is independent of necessary Choice and Infinity
groups.summary:
With the database’s strict-smallness definition, FP is independent over C + ☐Functional Choice + Axiom of Infinity (types e and t). Countably many S5 worlds supply the positive model; the negative direction was already recorded. More generally, for infinite W in external ZFC,

$$
\operatorname{FullS5}(W)\models\mathrm{FP}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 2^{|W|}=2^{\aleph_0}.
$$

A free-root model also satisfies FP and both quantified Infinity axioms while failing Intensional Choice. The cardinal criterion need not make W countable.

sections.title: Choice and completeness
sections.headline: Choice and Plenitude characterizations; countable completeness; no finite fixed-type Choice basis.

groups.title: Choice and Plenitude through sections and retractions
groups.summary:
Functional Choice is equivalent to Actuality plus pointwise sections of actual surjections; Plenitude is equivalent to Actuality plus pointwise retractions of actual injections. ☐Functional Choice is also equivalent to ☐Actuality plus the strong-section schema.

By contrast, requiring every actual injection between relational types to have a necessarily correct left inverse characterizes C5, without Actuality or Choice.

Over ☐Plenitude, ☐Functional Choice has an algebraic characterization: every admitted rigid Boolean subalgebra at every relational type, complete for families admitted by the model, has a [complete Boolean retraction](CANDIDATES_DK.md#complete-boolean-retractions). The necessary strong-section equivalence uses the Goodsell–Yli-Vakkuri No Pure Contingency theorem.
groups.certified_summary: The Functional Choice, Plenitude and ☐Functional Choice decompositions; the constituent directions of the C5/strong-retraction characterization.

groups.title: Countable completeness forces Frege finiteness at countable Boolean types
groups.summary: In C, a relational Boolean type that is countable in the model is countably complete exactly when it is Frege-finite. Countability in the model plus the matching Countable Boolean Completeness therefore implies Actuality, without Choice, Infinity, BF, ND or Plenitude.

groups.title: Functional Choice and ☐Functional Choice have no finite fixed-type basis
groups.summary: Neither Functional Choice nor ☐Functional Choice is equivalent over C to any finite list of pure fixed-type sentences. Selector strength forms a strict hierarchy as the available types increase. The proposed axioms may be arbitrary pure sentences, not merely Choice instances. This does not exclude finite stronger theories or finitely many unbounded type schemata.

sections.title: Arithmetic and analysis
sections.headline: Arithmetic conservation and reflection; Max’s proposed arithmetic equality and predecessor obstruction; rigid real structures.

groups.title: ☐Functional Choice and ☐Plenitude have the same ordinary arithmetic
groups.summary: Over C with Axiom of Infinity (types e and t), replacing ☐Plenitude by ☐Functional Choice adds no ordinary first-order arithmetic theorems. Both have the arithmetic consequences of C plus numerical noncollapse at e, and this remains true after adding ☐Axiom of Infinity (type σ) at every admitted σ. This establishes arithmetic conservation, not higher-order or modal conservation.

groups.title: Pure SP proves true Π₂ arithmetic, with a sharp conditional boundary
groups.summary: Under the specified pure Frege translation, pure SP proves every standard-true Π₂ arithmetic sentence. More generally, proofs in C plus numerical noncollapse of every standard numeral instance of P yield the universal numerical closure of P in SP. If SP is consistent, some true Π₃ sentence remains unprovable. This is a one-step reflection principle, not an iterated ω-rule for SP.

groups.title: Proposed exact arithmetic strength of pure Maximalism
groups.summary:
The proposed equality says that pure Maximalism proves exactly the ordinary first-order arithmetic consequences of the positive packages’ common arithmetic theory together with all standard-true Π₁ sentences.

$$
\operatorname{Th}_{\mathrm{arith}}(\operatorname{Max}(C))=\operatorname{Cn}\bigl(T_{\mathrm{arith}}\cup\mathrm{True}_{\Pi_1}\bigr).
$$

Here $T_{\mathrm{arith}}$ is the [common arithmetic theory](#arithmetic-comparison), $\mathrm{True}_{\Pi_1}$ means standard-true Π₁ sentences, and $\operatorname{Cn}$ is first-order deductive closure. The upper inclusion still awaits independent review.

groups.title: Maximalism forbids a numerical predecessor operation
groups.summary: At every admitted counting type, pure Maximalism refutes an operation sending each Frege successor back to its predecessor, without an Infinity or consistency premise. Yet a total single-valued predecessor graph is available: a functional arithmetic relation need not be representable by an intensional operation.

groups.title: Rigid Comprehension stabilizes a possible real structure
groups.summary: Over C5 plus ☐Rigid Comprehension, a possible real structure at a fixed type has a rigid representative that is necessarily a real structure. Represented powers can be supplied at any prescribed finite list of arities. The initial possibility premise is retained; completeness ranges over subproperties admitted by the model.

sections.title: Strong Possibility and language
sections.headline: Universal identities, named domains, signature extensions and finite Boolean ranks.

groups.title: Strong Possibility is an exact universal-identity theory
groups.summary: Pure Strong Possibility is equivalent over C to all closed pure universal finite-Boolean-identity sentences individually consistent with Max. Assuming Max is consistent, SP is consistent exactly when Max has the specified restricted finite-disjunction property for existential finite-Boolean-identity sentences. The criterion is proved; the required disjunction property remains unresolved.

groups.title: SP fixes the actual domain from the number of individual names
groups.summary: If Σ has exactly u < ∞ individual constant symbols, SP(Σ) entails exactly max(1,u) actual individuals; when u is positive, the names enumerate the domain bijectively. SP(pure) therefore entails one actual individual. This does not assert necessary exhaustion or exhaustion by infinitely many names.

groups.title: An exact finite-signature boundary and an infinite-reserve contrast
groups.summary:
For a proper extension of finite signatures Σ ⊊ Σ′, Max(Σ′) preserves every Max(Σ)-consistent old-language condition exactly when Σ has no individual names and the extension adds one individual name and no relational constants.

If Σ already has infinitely many constants at every type where Σ′ adds them, both Max(Σ′) and SP(Σ′) are conservative over the old-language theories. The fresh-name supply changes the answer; this does not assert that every old model admits an expansion.

groups.title: Pointed logical possibilities determine finite Boolean ranks
groups.summary:
For a closed pure proposition A, consider the complete consistent theories extending C(a)+A, with one fresh individual name a. Max is consistent with “there are no k+1 disjoint nonzero subpropositions of A” exactly when there are at most k such theories. If there are exactly k, SP(pure) forces the Boolean interval below A to have k atoms and 2ᵏ elements.

This extends the atom classification to every finite rank. Here k is a fixed finite number; the result does not establish consistency of SP.

sections.title: Model theory and computational complexity
sections.headline: Computational thresholds, exact model degrees, standard numbers and completion spaces.

groups.title: Theoremhood and model construction have successive jump thresholds
A complete theory has a model of exactly its computational degree
groups.summary: Every supplied complete consistent pure theory Γ extending C has a countable model of exactly Γ’s Turing degree, uniformly constructed from Γ. The construction preserves its exact pure theory. Together with reversible coding into completions, this realizes every degree in the positive and Max classes in the preceding table. These are degrees across models of a theory, not copies of one fixed model.

groups.title: Standard natural numbers impose a much stronger computational barrier
groups.summary:
Requiring the Frege numbers to be exactly the standard numerals changes the comparison sharply. With numerical noncollapse, every adequate standard-number code computes every hyperarithmetical real and is itself nonhyperarithmetical. Yet, for the positive packages with the specified Infinity assumptions and for Max, some standard codes lie strictly below Kleene’s O, and there is no least solution degree. Exactly the hyperarithmetical reals are computable from every standard code.

For those standard-model classes, finite-condition satisfiability is $\Sigma^1_1$-complete and validity is $\Pi^1_1$-complete. These are semantic restrictions; the corresponding SP claims require a standard SP model, whose existence is unresolved.

sections.title: Abstraction and infinitary extensions
sections.headline: Lambda-free reconstruction, beta eta conversion, Infinitary Comprehension and full standard models.

groups.title: Lambda-free reconstruction and contextual beta eta conversion
groups.summary:
An explicit classical applicative calculus with equality, quantifier binders, primitive ☐, K, theorem-only necessitation, all-relational Intensionality and uniform strong comprehension has exactly C’s consequences in its original language, including open contexts and assumptions. A conservative named extension reconstructs arbitrary C terms. No Choice, BF or Infinity premise is added.

Separately, on raw typed lambda syntax, beta identity at every relational output type plus application congruence and the theorem-only fresh-variable rule derives eta, lambda congruence and all contextual beta eta conversion. Positive-arity Intensionality supplies that rule; nullary Intensionality is unnecessary for this separate conversion theorem.

groups.title: Endpoint separation and boxed Infinitary Comprehension characterize full standard models
groups.summary:
Finite instances reconstruct abstraction, so no separate finitary-comprehension or λ-closure axiom is required. Endpoint separation recovers C5 + Atomicity (type t). The initial observer qualification needs strict Boolean and quantifier preservation; the translated equality clauses follow in the reconstructed theory. Whole-operation preservation remains expressible without λ notation.

The resulting hierarchy contains every proposition profile and every operation at an admitted relational-output type. The representation is provable in ZF, with Infinity and Extensionality left optional.

principle.statement: Over the λ-free base of H, full typed endpoint separation together with boxed Infinitary Comprehension characterizes full standard relational hierarchies in ZF:
principle.formal: \exists R^{\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_n t}\,\Box\forall x_1\cdots x_n\,\bigl(R[\bar x]\leftrightarrow A\bigr).
principle.scope: A is an arbitrary set-sized infinitary matrix with unrestricted simultaneous typed parameters; the bound tuple is finite and may be empty. The selected axioms are closed under necessitation.

groups.title: Infinitary formation changes named exhaustion and arithmetic
groups.summary:
For a signature with countably many individual names, admitting a predicate that holds exactly of individuals different from every name supplies the named-exhaustion reflection argument. A separate construction proves the needed Max-eligibility for an explicit semantic reference theory T_d; the corresponding SP(T_d) entails exactly countably many actual individuals. It does not prove SP(T_d) consistent or give the same result for an unspecified infinitary calculus.

A different addition—one countable numeral abstraction—makes the Frege number field standard at points satisfying numerical noncollapse and conflicts with Max referenced to finitary C. Infinitary assertions, term formation and inference therefore have different consequences.

sections.title: Evaluation and separating operators
sections.headline: Evaluator strengths, uniform selection, diagonal characters and symmetry.

groups.title: Six strictly different strengths of actual-truth evaluation
groups.summary:
For $E^{tt}$, correct evaluation means

$$
\operatorname{Eval}(E):=\forall p^t\, .\,(p\to Ep=\top)\land(\neg p\to Ep=\bot).
$$

The following requirements form a strict hierarchy over C, with each row stronger than the preceding one.

| Requirement | Equivalent principle |
|---|---|
| $\exists f^{tt}\, .\,\forall p^t\, .\,p\leftrightarrow fp=f\top$ | Actuality |
| $\exists E^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Eval}(E)$ | ND + Actuality |
| $\exists E^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Eval}(E)\land\bigl(\Box\forall p^t\, .\,Ep=\top\lor Ep=\bot\bigr)$ | Gallin Extensional Comprehension; equivalently ND + Strong Actuality |
| $\exists!E^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Eval}(E)$ | C5 + Actuality |
| $\Box\exists E^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Eval}(E)$, equivalently $\Box\exists!E^{tt}\, .\,\operatorname{Eval}(E)$ | ☐Plenitude |
| $\exists E^{tt}\, .\,\Box\operatorname{Eval}(E)$ | Extensionality |

The last two rows separate an evaluator available at each world from one fixed evaluator correct at every world. Uniqueness in the fourth row is among all evaluators correct at the current world. The third row already gives Boolean and quantifier identities for current predicates; the stronger ☐∀F law remains unresolved.

Actuality alone also interprets extensional Henkin higher-order logic over all current individuals. Represented relations and quantified Infinity transfer exactly, and Relational Choice supplies ordinary Choice in this interpretation. The construction makes no claim that its domains persist at other worlds.

groups.title: Uniform evaluator selection measures well-orderability and Choice
groups.summary: Over C + ☐Plenitude, one admitted operator choosing, for each nonzero proposition p, a complete bivalent evaluator sending p to ⊤ exists exactly when the world atoms admit a represented well-order. Requiring such selectors at every relational type is equivalent to ☐Functional Choice. The propositional requirement and all-type Intensional Choice are independent over C + ☐Plenitude. Here completeness means preservation of all admitted rigid meets; these evaluators take only ⊥ and ⊤ as values.

groups.title: Diagonal characters characterize ND + Atomicity at type t
groups.summary:
A diagonal character preserves ⊥ and negation, takes only ⊤/⊥ values, and accepts

$$
w_E:=\forall p^t\, .\,Ep\to p.
$$

Separation by such characters is equivalent to ND (type t) + Atomicity (type t); neither BF nor Choice is needed.

For the stronger logical-observer schema, see [Logical Observer Separation](#logical-observers).

groups.title: Symmetry controls the representation of observers
groups.summary:
Over C + ☐ND (type t) + Actuality, propositional separation by observers preserving Boolean operations and quantification at t as composite operation identities is equivalent to Atomicity (type t). Atomicity supplies the corresponding observers at each fixed quantifier type.

In the specified symmetric ideally-full models with closed target symmetry groups, an arrow’s truth-evaluation map is representable exactly when the transported stabilizer of some finite set is contained in the target symmetry group. A representing observer can preserve Boolean operations and both quantifiers as operation identities.

The ordered symmetry construction separates these demands: Boolean observer separation holds at every world, and ☐BF holds, while quantifier separation fails at type e. This gives a route to studying observers through permutation groups, beyond the atomic sufficient conditions.
groups.certified_summary: The propositional Atomicity characterization at t; simultaneous separation for every finite list of quantifier types under C5 + Atomicity (type t), with the converse under C5 + Actuality.

sections.title: Logical observers
sections.headline: The hierarchy over H; representation, adjoints, reversibility and separating models.

groups.title: Logical observer separation: a branching implication map
groups.summary:
Requiring separation by **logical observers → endpoint observers → a unique observer** leads respectively to C + BF, C5 + Atomicity (type t), and Extensionality over H. Under Extensionality, truth is itself an endpoint-valued observer. Over C, every arrow below is strict:

$$
\small\text{Extensionality}\ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{C5}+\mathrm{Atomicity}_t\ \Rightarrow\ \Box\mathrm{OS}\ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{OS}\ \Rightarrow\ \mathrm{BF}.
$$

Reversible logical separation implies No Pure Contingency without atoms or Actuality. The [observer section](#h-observer-separation) and [full map](proofs/h-observer-space/GRAPH.md) give the other branches and separating models.
groups.certified_summary: H + OS ⇒ C + BF in the equivalent formulation with explicit endpoint identities

groups.title: Preservation, representation and logical observers
groups.summary:
The [dedicated page](proofs/h-observer-space/GRAPH.md) develops the map from H, with exact premises, diagrams, proofs and countermodels. Its main results are:

- **Preservation and higher types.** For the finite family of independent primitive clauses, implication between separation principles is exactly reverse inclusion of clauses. Full typed separation factors into propositional separation plus Functionality.
- **Reversibility.** Separation by reversible logical observers (Rev) implies C5 + ☐OS + No Pure Contingency. Both chains Rev ⇒ SurjSep ⇒ OS and Rev ⇒ SplitMono ⇒ OS are strict; SurjSep and SplitMono require surjective observers and admitted qualified left inverses, respectively, and are incomparable. Over C5, SurjSep is Rev.
- **The endpoint boundary.** OS + Plenitude at (t,t) is equivalent over H to endpoint separation, hence to C5 + Atomicity (type t). Reversibility can hold in atomless models; one atom raises it to endpoint separation.
- **Canonical adjoints.** Over C5, every logical observer qualified at t has admitted order adjoints. These characterize injection, surjection and reversibility. A Boolean observer commutes with necessity exactly when it is injective.
- **Limits of combination and persistence.** Separate preservation requirements need not combine. SurjSep entails neither ☐OS nor ☐BF, even though an individual observer’s surjectivity persists over C + BF (type t).
- **Exact characterizations.** Over C5, Rev is characterized by its fixed propositions. Laws on the whole reversible group give sharp finite bounds; internally finite observer families give exact finiteness characterizations. [Statements and proofs](proofs/h-observer-space/GRAPH.md#reversibility-and-the-invariant-proposition-algebra).

The [detailed map and research frontier](proofs/h-observer-space/MAP.md) also cover weaker connective fragments, normalization, character extension and atomless order models.

**Main unresolved question:** does injective logical separation imply separation by logical observers with logical left inverses? The converse holds; this direction remains open over H and over C5. [Exact question and positive cases](CONJECTURES.md#observer-strength).

sections.title: Worlds, profiles and probability
sections.headline: Profile realization, world orbits, faithful probability and its type ceiling.

groups.title: Profile richness and Functional Choice are separate requirements
groups.summary: Over ☐Plenitude, the world-representation results support consistent individual profile-realization strengthenings. Nominal models realize every finite supported richness rank while failing Functional Choice. Unrestricted relational-input realization instead meets a diagonal obstruction; it must not be identified with individual or finitely supported realization.

groups.title: World orbits determine propositional Dedekind infinity
groups.summary:
In the specified finite-support permutation models, propositions admit an injective nonsurjective operation exactly when there are infinitely many world orbits. Even infinitely many worlds can form just one orbit.

On atom worlds, ☐Intensional Choice at every admitted type coexists with the necessary failure of this operational Dedekind infinity. This concerns operations on propositions, not the quantified Frege Axiom of Infinity.

groups.title: Faithful probability has an exact finite-fibre condition and type ceiling
groups.summary: Over C + ☐Plenitude + Axiom of Infinity (type e), faithful probability is equivalent to admitted finite-fibre numerical labelling of world atoms. Countable Choice for finite fields strengthens this to countability in the model. Higher-type probability faces a finiteness obstruction.
